 ORDER This petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following reliefs:-

And order dated 28.03.2019 passed by (S.D.O.) Sub- divisional officer, Sub division Singrouli,
M.P. Annexure p/2 and order dated 02.08.2022 passed by commissioner Rewa,
Division Rewa, M.P. Annexure P/3., in the interest of justice.
(II) It is, therefore, prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondents to record the name of petitioner in all revenue records, in the interest of justice.
(III) Any other direction/order, which deemed fit and proper looking to the facts and circumstances of the case."
2. It is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the owner of land bearing Khasra No.816, area 0.72 acre situated in Village Nawanagar, Tahsil and District Singrauli.
0.50 acre of land was acquired by the NCL and compensation has been paid and there is no dispute with regard to the compensation.
Since, the remaining 0.22 acres of land was not acquired, therefore, the petitioner is entitled to remain in possession of the said remaining land i.e. 0.22 acre.

Accordingly,
the petitioner filed an application for mutation of his name in respect of Khasra No. 816, area 0.22 acre only.

The Tehsildar called the report and it was submitted by the authority that only 0.50 acre of land was acquired by the NCL and by mistake the name of the NCL was mutated in respect of the entire 0.72 acre of land.

However, the application filed by the petitioner for mutation of his name Manmati vs The State Of Mp on 13 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176011743/
2 was rejected by the Tehsildar by order dated 11.09.2021 on the ground that the matter pertains to acquisition.

sentences.text: The petitioner filed an appeal which too was dismissed by the SDO.

3. Being aggrieved by the order passed by the SDO, the petitioner preferred Second Appeal which has been dismissed by the Commissioner, Rewa, Division Rewa by order dated 02.08.2022 with an observation that since the petitioner is seeking release of land from acquisition, therefore, she should have moved an application before the Collector and no relief can be granted by the Tehsildar.
4. Challenging the orders passed by the authorities, it is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner had never asked for relieving of her land from acquisition.

Her case is that she was the owner of 0.72 acre of land forming part of Khasra No. 816, situated in Village Nawanager,
Tehsil and District Singrauli out of which only 0.50 acre of land was acquired.

However, by mistake,
the name of the NCL was mutated in respect of entire 0.72 acre of land.
Even NCL had submitted its reply before the authorities giving its no objection in case if the name of the petitioner is mutated in respect of the remaining un- acquired 0.22 acre of land.
The said reply was conveniently ignored by the authorities.
It is submitted that in fact it is not a case for release of land from acquisition but it is a case of correction of revenue entries.
5. This Court by order dated 06.04.2023 had issued notice to the respondents.

6. The respondent No. 5 has taken the following stands:-
"3.

That, the correct fact is that the Government of India through its competent authority has acquired 0.50 acre of land under the Coal Bearing Areas Act of Kh.No.816 having total area 0.72 acre by publishing notice U/s 9 of the CBA Act on 04.02.1982, the amount of compensation has been paid to petitioner / owner of land.

entities.text: Coal Bearing Areas Act of Kh.
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The NCL Management is only in possession of the land which is acquired, rest of the land is used by the petitioner and has no concern with NCL.
4.

That, it is submitted that before the revenue authorities NCL Management has taken its stand as stated above, however it was the revenue authorities who have appreciated the facts as per their own understanding and have passed the impugned order, therefore they have to justified and explain.

5. That, it is submitted that the other respondents are required to explain the passing of impugned order and no relief can be granted against the NCL, the matter is between petitioner and the revenue authorities who are the best judge and custodian of the records, therefore they are required to satisfy and answer the grounds and facts with prayer advance by petitioner."
7. From the return filed by the NCL, it is clear that the stand of the NCL is that it had acquired only 0.50 acre of land and has no concern with the remaining 0.22 acre of land.

Even otherwise, the NCL had filed its reply before the Tehsildar which reads as under:-

8. It is really surprising that in spite of the specific stand taken by the NCL, the authorities have misunderstood the case and were under impression that it is the case for release of land from acquisition.
In fact, it is a case of correction of revenue entries.

9. In view of the stand taken by the NCL before the Tehsildar, Tehsil and District Singrauli as well as the return filed before this Court, the orders dated 02.08.2022, 28.03.2019 and 11.09.2001 are hereby set aside.
The Tehsildar, Singrauli is directed to decide the application filed by the petitioner as an application for correction of revenue entries and not an application for release of land from acquisition.

10. If, it is found that the petitioner is the owner of 0.22 acres of land forming part of Khasra No.
816, then the name of the petitioner be recorded in respect of the land which was not acquired for/by NCL.
11.
With aforesaid direction, the petition is finally disposed of.
